title: Bound durable rate backfill so order and shipment sync cannot starve

acceptanceCriteria.description: Order and shipment cadence work has priority over every rate-backfill source, while rate backfill retains the one canonical ShipStation advisory lane and runs in bounded two-order durable chunks.
Queue handler cancellation reaches rate-backfill DB/provider work, and non-cooperative work cannot falsely acknowledge cancellation or release the lane before fail-closed worker recovery.
No successor generation overlaps live work from an old generation; deterministic chunk IDs, durable cursor state, and generation reconciliation make retry and restart idempotent.
Repeated cadence and deferral wake-ups coalesce into one persisted active rate-backfill generation, and completed chunks resume from a durable keyset cursor without rerating the completed prefix.
Under continuous worst-priority rate pressure, every simulated three-minute order and shipment cadence job completes within the documented thirteen-minute freshness budget.

Persisted worker status and backend health expose active lane job, generation, start, age, timeout/deadline, and order/shipment completion watermarks; stale watermarks or an over-age lane are non-green while healthy cadence remains green.
The focused PS-436 proof, adjacent sync/rate/health suites, all 53 mandatory source-of-truth guards, strict TypeScript checks, and the production frontend build pass at the exact current stable SHA.

Verification made zero database connections, live provider calls, label/postage purchases, marketplace notifications, inventory movements, or production order/shipment mutations; awaiting-only selection and shipped/cancelled protections remain intact.

sotBypass.details: The existing pg-boss/advisory lane remains authoritative. Routes and schedulers only admit or read durable work, provider/DB waits receive the queue signal, and no frontend timer, second scheduler, route-local queue, resolver, or fallback timestamp became authoritative.

evidence.proves: The offline executable proof uses real admission priorities and continuation/coalescing owners. It coalesces 101 cadence wakes, resumes deterministic two-order chunks, and completes all 40 simulated operational cadence jobs under continuous worst-case rate pressure with a maximum age of 60 seconds against a 780-second freshness budget.

An aborted but unsettled DB/provider promise remains unsettled, the shared lane continues to block order and shipment successors until the fail-closed decision, stale first-chunk wakes join the persisted continuation, and the same completed chunk deterministically derives one continuation ID.

Two injected non-cooperative cancellation scenarios remain fenced through bounded acknowledgement grace. Cooperative provider work observes parent abort; an ignoring provider cannot fabricate settlement, its late response is rejected, and the canonical queue path requests status closeout then worker termination while the advisory lane is still held so durable pg-boss recovery cannot overlap old writes.

migrations.rollbackPlan: No schema rollback is required. Use a reviewed forward revert of the stable-equivalent PS-436 runtime commits 26ac3d86f4fd1c5bc8030ebb3cc7d4a1d1b247a8 and 8d2c5e416f8728554f6b82b3108874776a55945c, then redeploy a reviewed compatible stable artifact. Preserve existing settings and pg-boss rows; do not delete durable history or mutate orders/shipments.

rollback.strategy: If post-deploy syncFreshness becomes non-green, stop new rate cadence admission, allow or restart the worker through the existing bounded recovery path, verify no active old generation remains, and deploy a reviewed forward revert of 26ac3d86f4fd1c5bc8030ebb3cc7d4a1d1b247a8 and 8d2c5e416f8728554f6b82b3108874776a55945c. Preserve durable generation/settings and pg-boss evidence, and never rewrite order/shipment history.
